clauses.reason: This clause adds the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Domestic and International Business to section 305 of Executive Order No. 10973. Executive Order 12163 (signed September 29, 1979; 44 FR 56673) states in section 1-903(a) that the following are revoked: "(1) Executive Order No. 10973 of November 3,1961, as amended;" and in section 1-905 "The provisions of this order shall become effective as of October 1,1979." Its section 1-505 establishes a Development Loan Committee and its section 1-506 a Development Coordination Committee, which are new committees under that order and are not treated as keeping this order in force. Executive Order 11579 section 4(d) (1971) supersedes Executive Order No. 10973 only insofar as provisions conflict; it names no section of this order's insertion and no source shows it extinguished the amendment, so it is not an end. Executive Order 11841 adds a separate section 306 to the same parent and does not touch section 305.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (33 FR 10625, issue of July 26, 1968) is Executive Order 11417, adding an Assistant Secretary of Commerce to the membership of the Development Loan Committee. I read the whole order, a single operative paragraph: Executive Order No. 10973, as amended, "is hereby further amended by inserting in section 305" the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Domestic and International Business. The held text layer also carries neighbouring Commerce regulations on the same pages, which are not part of the order. End: the parent was revoked by Executive Order 12163, effective October 1, 1979, Executive Order 12163 (signed September 29, 1979; 44 FR 56673) states in section 1-903(a) that the following are revoked: "(1) Executive Order No. 10973 of November 3,1961, as amended;" and in section 1-905 "The provisions of this order shall become effective as of October 1,1979." Its section 1-505 establishes a Development Loan Committee and its section 1-506 a Development Coordination Committee, which are new committees under that order and are not treated as keeping this order in force. Executive Order 11579 section 4(d) (1971) supersedes Executive Order No. 10973 only insofar as provisions conflict; it names no section of this order's insertion and no source shows it extinguished the amendment, so it is not an end. The amendment lived only as text inside section 305 of the parent, so it ended with the parent on 1979-10-01. Other held amendments of the parent (Executive Orders 11685, 11816, 11959 and 12118) were checked and do not mention section 305 or this insertion; Executive Order 11841 adds a different section 306. The machine search lists these as chain items only.
